issues.sym: The transmission suddenly won't go into Reverse, slips or flares in some gears, gets stuck in a low gear, or shudders. Some cars eventually lose drive entirely and have to be towed.
issues.why: A wave plate (a spring-like clutch part) inside the 6-speed automatic can crack and break. GM issued special coverage (bulletin 14404) for 2007-2009 Auras with the 6-speed, which includes the 3.6L V6 cars and the 2009 2.4L cars. That coverage was 10 years or 120,000 miles and has now run out.
issues.next: If Reverse goes missing or the transmission starts slipping, stop driving it hard and get it diagnosed. A shop can often replace the broken clutch part during a teardown; driving on it can turn a repair into a full replacement.

issues.sym: Check engine light, often together with the traction control light, and timing codes such as P0008 or P0017. Some engines run rough or rattle, especially on a cold start.
issues.why: The timing chains on the 3.6L V6 stretch early, often between about 45,000 and 85,000 miles. Long oil change intervals and low oil make it worse.
issues.next: Don't ignore a check engine light with timing codes. Have a shop confirm chain stretch and replace all the chains, guides and tensioners with the updated kit. A chain that jumps can wreck the engine.

issues.sym: The driver seat rocks, leans toward the console, or drops suddenly, sometimes with a loud snap. A bar may poke through the cushion and the power seat may stop adjusting.
issues.why: Welds on the driver seat frame and its cross members crack and break with use. Owners report frames breaking again even after replacement.
issues.next: A loose seat is a safety problem in a crash. Have the frame inspected and replaced, and keep the seat fully lowered until it is fixed.

issues.sym: A shaking steering wheel or pulsing pedal when braking, squealing or grinding, and pads wearing unevenly. Many owners see it by about 30,000 miles.
issues.why: The front rotors run hot and warp early, and some owners report pad material building up and scoring the rotors. It is the single most reported problem on the 2007 Aura.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replacing pads and rotors together usually fixes it; good-quality rotors last longer than resurfaced ones.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working or cycle by themselves
issues.sym: One or more doors won't lock or unlock with the fob, switch or key, or the locks cycle on their own while driving or parked.
issues.why: The door lock actuator motors wear out. In some cars the body control module is blamed instead.
issues.next: Have the shop test the actuator in each problem door before replacing the body control module, since actuators are the more common and cheaper fix.

issues.t: Knock in the steering when turning
issues.sym: A knock or clunk you can feel in the steering wheel when turning, especially at low speed or over bumps.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft between the column and the rack develops play. Owners report dealers installing a redesigned shaft; lubricating it often only helps for a while.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and rack inspected. Ask a dealer whether an updated shaft is available for your car.

issues.t: Engine Power Reduced and traction control warning
issues.sym: The Engine Power Reduced or Service Traction message appears, the car will barely accelerate, and other warning lights may come on. Some owners report stalling.
issues.why: There is no single cause. Body control module faults, wiring and connector problems and timing chain codes have all been found to trigger it.
issues.next: Pull over somewhere safe if power drops. Have all stored codes read from every module, not just the engine computer, so the real cause is found.

issues.t: Service Hybrid message and lost hybrid assist (recall)
issues.sym: A Service Hybrid message and check engine light appear, auto-stop stops working and fuel economy drops. The car still runs on the gas engine.
issues.why: Problems in the 36-volt hybrid battery pack can cause a voltage imbalance that shuts the hybrid system off. GM recalled Green Line hybrids to replace the battery cassettes or the battery pack and reprogram the engine computer.
issues.next: Have a GM dealer check your VIN for open hybrid battery recalls. If none are open, the hybrid battery originally had an 8-year/100,000-mile warranty.

issues.t: Hybrid battery overheating or sensor fault drains the car
issues.sym: Hybrid warnings come on, the car stops charging, and it eventually goes dead. A jump start may not keep it running. Codes in the P1A range are stored.
issues.why: The 36-volt battery pack behind the rear seat has temperature sensors and a cooling fan. If the pack overheats or a sensor or fan fails, the whole hybrid system shuts down, and the regular 12-volt battery is no longer charged.
issues.next: Don't keep jump-starting it. Have a shop with hybrid experience read the codes and check the battery fan, its air intake and the temperature sensors before condemning the battery.

issues.t: Squealing drive belt on hybrid models
issues.sym: Squealing or chirping from the engine belt, especially at auto-stop restarts or under acceleration.
issues.why: On the Green Line, the drive belt also starts the engine and adds electric assist, so it wears faster than on a normal car. The tensioner needs a special tool to service.
issues.next: Have the belt and tensioner checked for wear, alignment and tension. A worn belt can leave the car unable to restart after an auto-stop.

issues.sym: Cracks appear in the top of the dashboard.
issues.why: The dashboard plastic cracks with heat and age on some cars.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. A dash cover hides it; replacing the dash pad is expensive and not usually worth it.

issues.t: Brake lights may fail or come on by themselves (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights don't come on when you brake, or come on when you don't. Cruise control may not work or disengage, and stability control warnings may appear.
issues.why: Wear and corrosion in the brake light circuit at the body control module connector can cause these failures. GM recalled the cars (NHTSA 14V-252) to clean and grease the connector and secure the wiring.
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Shift cable can break so the gear shown isn't the real gear (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter may show Park while the transmission is still in gear, so the car can roll away after you get out.
issues.why: The transmission shift cable can fracture. GM recalled the cars (NHTSA 14V-224), and dealers fix the cable at no cost.
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Shift cable mounting tabs can break (recall)
issues.sym: The shift lever may not match the actual gear. You may be able to take the key out while the car is not in Park, and it may not restart.
issues.why: Plastic tabs that hold the shift cable to its bracket can fracture and let the cable come loose. GM recalled the cars (NHTSA 12V-460).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power steering assist (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes heavy, especially at low speeds and when parking, and a steering warning may come on.
issues.why: The electric power steering can lose assist. GM recalled the cars (NHTSA 14V-153), and dealers repair the steering system at no cost.
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Car may roll away after shifting to Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car may not restart, or may roll after you leave it, because it is not fully in Park.
issues.why: A shift cable part may not have been fully seated at the factory. GM recalled the cars (NHTSA 09V-073).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.
